source.note: The lagna lord without strength, Jupiter in a kendra or a trikona, and a malefic in the sixth, eighth or twelfth: the middle span, from the 33rd year to the 70th. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.
Benefics in a kendra, and the lagna lord joined with them or aspected by Jupiter: the full span. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.
The lagna lord in a kendra, joined with or aspected by Jupiter and Venus: long life. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.
Three grahas exalted, and the lord of the eighth in the lagna with no malefic there: long life. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.

Saturn or the lord of the eighth joined with a graha in its exaltation: long life. v. 88's three in the eighth in exaltation, a friend's sign and their own varga is not built. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.

Malefics in the third, sixth and eleventh, benefics in kendras or trikonas, and the lagna lord strong: long life. The nodes are left out of the malefics: they stand six houses apart, and no two of the third, sixth and eleventh are, so with them the verse could never hold. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.

Benefics together in the sixth, seventh or eighth, and malefics in the third, sixth and eleventh: long life. The nodes are left out of the malefics: they stand six houses apart, and no two of the third, sixth and eleventh are, so with them the verse could never hold. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.

Malefics in the eleventh and the sixth and the lagna lord in a kendra: long life, the majority of astrologers agree. The verse's second figure is lost in the OCR and not built; v. 93's chain of lords is not built. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.
A dual lagna whose lord is in a kendra, its own sign, its exaltation or its moolatrikona: long life and fortune. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.
A dual lagna, and two malefics in kendras from its lord: long life. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.
The Sun, Saturn and Mars in movable navamshas, Jupiter and Venus in fixed ones, and the rest in dual ones: a hundred years. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 translation.

The Sun, Jupiter and Mars each in a navamsha of Saturn's, or in the ninth and its own navamsha, and strong, with the strong Moon in the lagna: life to the end of the yuga, and wealth. The commentary quotes the same figure from the Hora Prakasha. Read in the Sanskrit with Kapileshvara Shastri's commentary (Chowkhamba), the pages V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 scan lacks.

Jupiter and Saturn in one navamsha, both in the ninth or both in the tenth, aspected by benefics, and the Sun rising, which the commentary reads as the Sun in the lagna: a long-lived ascetic. Read in the Sanskrit with Kapileshvara Shastri's commentary (Chowkhamba), the pages V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 scan lacks.

No malefic in the trines (the fifth and ninth, by the commentary), no benefic in a kendra and no malefic in the eighth: the native is like an immortal, which the section's heading calls likeness to the gods. v. 101 names its grahas "from Saturn to Mars", three in the order of the spheres or four in the weekdays', and is not built (C396). Read in the Sanskrit with Kapileshvara Shastri's commentary (Chowkhamba), the pages V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 scan lacks.

The last part of Aries rising with Jupiter or Venus in it, the Moon in Taurus's middle (fifth) navamsha and Mars in his Simhasana amsha: countless years through mantras, the heading's asankhya ayu. "The last part" is read as the last navamsha, the measure the verse gives the Moon. Each name is the commentary's count of the graha's own vargas of the ten (Gopura four, Simhasana five, Paravata six, Devaloka seven, and eight by ch. 1's ladder, which names nine Airavata), a varga its own when it holds the graha's exaltation, moolatrikona or own sign, or in the navamsha its rasi sign, as ch. 1 vv. 44 to 46 count them without BPHS ch. 6's arudha-kendra lords (C396). Read in the Sanskrit with Kapileshvara Shastri's commentary (Chowkhamba), the pages V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 scan lacks.

Saturn in his Devaloka amsha, Mars in his Paravata amsha and Jupiter in his Simhasana amsha in the lagna: the native is like a sage, the heading's muni-samatva, read as the divine life BPHS ch. 43 gives the ascetic. Only Jupiter is asked in the lagna, as both glosses read it. Each name is the commentary's count of the graha's own vargas of the ten (Gopura four, Simhasana five, Paravata six, Devaloka seven, and eight by ch. 1's ladder, which names nine Airavata), a varga its own when it holds the graha's exaltation, moolatrikona or own sign, or in the navamsha its rasi sign, as ch. 1 vv. 44 to 46 count them without BPHS ch. 6's arudha-kendra lords (C396). Read in the Sanskrit with Kapileshvara Shastri's commentary (Chowkhamba), the pages V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 scan lacks.

Jupiter in a kendra in his Gopura amsha, Venus in a trine (the fifth or ninth, by the commentary) in his Paravata amsha, and Cancer rising: life to the yuga's end. Each name is the commentary's count of the graha's own vargas of the ten (Gopura four, Simhasana five, Paravata six, Devaloka seven, and eight by ch. 1's ladder, which names nine Airavata), a varga its own when it holds the graha's exaltation, moolatrikona or own sign, or in the navamsha its rasi sign, as ch. 1 vv. 44 to 46 count them without BPHS ch. 6's arudha-kendra lords (C396). Read in the Sanskrit with Kapileshvara Shastri's commentary (Chowkhamba), the pages V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1932 scan lacks.
